trial_court: Principal Senior Civil Judge, Narasaraopet - O.S.No.297 of 1988
case_name: M.Ramakrishna Prasad. 2Ors vs K.Singaiah, Vijayawada6 Ors
facts_of_case: The appellants sued for partition of properties, claiming they were joint family properties with the respondents. The respondents remained ex parte. The suit was instituted when the appellants were minors and continued after they attained majority.

legal_principles.principle: Once an order is passed by the competent authority determining excess holding and directing taking over the excess lands, it shall be deemed that such excess holding has been surrendered.
legal_principles.held: Asserting that once an order is passed by the competent authority viz., Land Reforms Tribunal determining the excess holding and directing taking over the excess lands, it shall be deemed that such excess holding has been surrendered by the 1st respondent.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party claiming that an order has not been complied with to establish non-compliance.
legal_principles.held: Asserting that so called excess lands attributed MVR,J to the 1st respondent were never surrendered, the learned counsel contended that in view of the amendment brought out by Central Act 15/1997 (Urban Land (Ceiling and regulation) Repeal Act, 1999, since the possession of these lands is established to remain with the appellants and the 1st respondent.

outcome.final_order: The final court order confirmed the decree and judgment of the trial court.

keywords: Latin maxim: Nemo dat quod non habet
